sign.title: Sign a GIF — GifOS
sign.heading: Sign a GIF 🛡️
sign.lead: Prove you made an app GIF. Signing binds these exact app bytes to your domain or email, so GifOS shows “Signed by you” to anyone who opens it. Everything happens in your browser — no upload, no account. Your app's saved data is never part of the signature, so it stays valid as people use the app.
sign.drop.prompt: Drop your .gif here, or click to choose one
sign.domain.intro: Signs with an Ed25519 key you generate here. Publish the public half at {url} and anyone can verify — the key location is derived from the domain, so “Signed by it” means you control it.
sign.domain.label: Your domain
sign.domain.putAt: Put THIS at {url} (public — safe to share):
sign.domain.keepSafe: Keep the private key file safe — it's how you sign. Losing it just means generating a new one and re-publishing gifos.key.
sign.email.intro: Signs with your own OpenPGP key using your existing tools — Ed25519 and RSA (2048+) keys both work, and your private key never touches this page. Others verify against the copy of your key on {link}, so publish your key there first and confirm your email.
sign.email.label: Your email
sign.email.step2: Sign it with your PGP key (in a terminal):
sign.email.step3: Upload the .sig and download your signed GIF
sign.foot: Signing proves authorship, not safety. Anyone can strip a signature (the file just becomes anonymous), and a signature only says the contents are unchanged since signing. {back}
sign.msg.notGif: That is not a GIF file.
sign.msg.alreadySigned: Note: this GIF is already signed by {id}. Signing replaces it.
sign.msg.keyGenerated: New key generated. Download BOTH files below, publish gifos.key on your domain, keep the private key safe.
sign.msg.keyLoadFailed: Could not load that key file: {message}
sign.msg.signedDomain: Signed by {domain} — downloaded. Make sure gifos.key is live on your domain so others can verify.
sign.msg.statementDownloaded: Statement downloaded. Sign it with gpg (step 2), then upload the .sig.
sign.msg.signedEmail: Signed by {email} — downloaded. Publish your key on keys.openpgp.org so others can verify.
